_comment: Pinned organ->Brain usage-evidence contract for KURU decision 0028.
Every id below was observed from live organ output, not invented. Changing a
pin is a deliberate act: it means the organ's published contract really did
change and every consumer keyed on the old name must be updated in the same
commit. That is the whole point - an identifier rename should cost a reviewed
edit here, not eight releases of silently empty routing.

claude._why: the account-level session and weekly windows that bound every model

codex._why: five_hour is emitted on some plans and weekly on others; either satisfies the pin

_why_required: These are the exact two ids upstream renamed. They are pinned as REQUIRED,
not merely known, because the realized failure was a PARTIAL rename: four
of six ids survived, so any check asking only 'did some pinned id survive'
would have passed the very regression it existed to catch.
_why: These are the PUBLISHED normalized ids. Upstream renamed two of them
product:grokimagine -> product:imagine) with no major version change and
no deprecation. That rename is the realized failure this contract exists
to catch: identifier-drift fires the moment none of these appear.

cursor._why: commonly auth_required; absence of windows is not a decoder fault

kimi._why: not metered by any consumer here
